title.title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion
title.subtitle: Claim: a unital separable C*-algebra is $\mathcal Z$-stable exactly when its central sequence algebra has no characters

beats.text: Jiang–Su stability: the regularity behind the classification of C*-algebras
Claim: it holds exactly when the central sequence algebra has no characters

achievement.label: Kirchberg–Rørdam question (2015)
statement: A \cong A \otimes \mathcal Z \iff A_\omega \cap A' \text{ has no characters}
achievement.context: Before: partial results under extra hypotheses; Dadarlat–Toms asked about tensor powers (2009)
achievement.note: Also: infinite tensor powers without characters absorb $\mathcal Z$

verify.detail: The character criterion, for every free ultrafilter; the tensor-power result is not listed
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

plain: A simple test for when an algebra soaks up a special regularizing algebra: look for characters

steps: No characters means pieces that never commute, in any picture
Combine them into one element whose square is zero
Spread it over tensor powers: a dimension-drop algebra fits

voice.text: Absorbing the Jiang–Su algebra drives classification. When does an algebra absorb it?
Without characters, build a square-zero element and spread it across tensor powers.
Claimed: exactly when central sequences have no characters.
